title: Grade concept freshness from anchors and git, with seed and confirm verbs
action: Add the freshness grade to the knowledge bundle (D3 27ad96a5, D8 4148025d) exactly by the Grade rule and the Seeding paragraph in plan.md Approach. New module verbs/knowledge/freshness.rs exports: (1) `bundle_root(root, feature: Option<&str>) -> PathBuf` — the docs/knowledge directory of the checkout the command runs in, built the way drivers/close.rs `docs_root_for_feature` picks a granted worktree's tree (anchor: `pub(crate) fn docs_root_for_feature(root: &Path, feature: &str) -> PathBuf {`); every knowledge verb that reads or writes concepts (check, list, search, show, context, new, seed-anchors, confirm) resolves its bundle through it, so a command run inside a granted worktree reads and writes that worktree's docs tree; (2) `grade_bundle(checkout_root, concepts) -> BTreeMap<rel_path, Grade>` and `grade_concept(checkout_root, rel_path, bee: &Map<String, Value>) -> Grade` where `Grade { grade: confirmed|suspect|orphan|unverified, verified_at: Option<String>, verified_commit: Option<String>, anchors: Vec<String>, changed: Vec<String>, reason: Option<String> }` — the signature takes the bundle-relative path and the parsed `bee` map, not walk::Concept, so the session preamble's own Concept type can call it; implement the one-pass rule from plan.md: one `git log --format=%H --name-only --first-parent -m <oldest verified_commit>..HEAD` through verbs/worktree/git.rs `run_git` (anchor: `pub(crate) fn run_git(cwd: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> GitOut {`) plus one `git merge-base --is-ancestor <vc> HEAD` per distinct verified_commit, never a git call per anchor; a concept's repo path for the same-commit exemption is `docs/knowledge/<rel>`. Three frontmatter fields under `bee`: `anchors` (flat list), `verified_at` (ISO date), `verified_commit` (full sha); every write goes through the canonical emitter (frontmatter.rs `emit_scalar` / `is_plain_safe`) and a written file must report zero not_canonical. In check.rs, after the profile pass, grade every concept under areas/ only (never patterns/, never work/, never index.md) and emit: text summary line `freshness: <n> confirmed, <n> suspect, <n> orphan, <n> unverified`; `--json` object `freshness: {confirmed, suspect, orphan, unverified, rows: [{path, grade, verified_at, verified_commit, changed, reason}]}`; one profile WARNING per suspect concept (code `stale_anchor`, message naming the changed anchors and the remedy `bee knowledge confirm --id <bee.id>`) and per orphan concept (code `orphan_anchor`, naming the missing path and the remedy: fix bee.anchors); unverified is counted, never warned; when areas/ has concepts and none carries bee.anchors, print one NOTE `no concept carries bee.anchors — run bee knowledge seed-anchors once`. Two new single-token verbs routed in routing.rs (anchor: `"check" => run_check(flags, json, pre_json, t0),`) and declared in generated/registry_payload.json as `{name, invoke, description}` rows beside `knowledge.check` (round-trip the JSON keeping its byte format): `bee knowledge seed-anchors [--dry-run]` walks areas/ only and, for every concept with NO `bee.anchors` key, collects the backticked repo-relative paths in its body that exist under the checkout (same backtick-path shape `dangling_source_candidate` accepts), skipping any path under `.bee/`, `docs/`, or containing a `/generated/` segment; writes them as `bee.anchors`; sets `bee.verified_commit` to `git log -1 --format=%H -- docs/knowledge/<rel>` and `bee.verified_at` to that commit's ISO date (a concept with no commit gets anchors only); prints per-file counts and how many concepts got zero anchors. `bee knowledge confirm (--id <bee.id>)+ | --path <repo path>` stamps `verified_at` (today, UTC) and `verified_commit` (current HEAD of the checkout) on each named concept, or on every areas/ concept whose anchors contain --path; refusals, each naming its remedy: unknown id → `no concept with bee.id <id> — bee knowledge list`; concept with no anchors → `<path> has no bee.anchors — run bee knowledge seed-anchors or add anchors`; --path matching no concept → `no concept anchors <path>`; confirm never clears orphan and says so when the grade stays orphan. Extend tests/registry_dispatch.rs `every_namespace_the_dispatcher_serves_is_declared_in_the_registry` (anchor: `for verb in match_arm_verbs(&crate_src("devtools/mod.rs"), "pub fn try_native", 5) {`) to also scan verbs/knowledge/routing.rs's match arms as `bee knowledge <verb>`, so an undeclared knowledge verb fails the test. Tests red-first in knowledge/tests.rs on a fixture repo with real git commits: each of the four grades; anchor changed in a commit that also touched the concept → confirmed; a present sha that is not an ancestor of HEAD → unverified with a reason; a merge commit touching an anchor is seen; seed writes anchors and the baseline commit only where anchors are absent and the file stays canonical; confirm stamps both fields, handles --path, and each refusal names its remedy; a confirm run from a granted worktree writes the worktree's concept and leaves main untouched; check's --json carries the freshness object, the stale_anchor / orphan_anchor rows and the seed NOTE.

park.question: The semantic judge found the grade window wrong on merged branches (first-parent walk plus an octopus base that falls back to the whole range) and over the call budget. Which window rule should the rework implement?
park.answer: Owner direction, waggledance task t-ae0fad: the grade window must not depend on --first-parent and must never fall back to the whole common-base range when a verified_commit sits on a merged branch. This replaces the --first-parent -m wording in the cell action and in plan.md Approach. Contract: a concept's window is exactly the commits reachable from HEAD and not reachable from its own verified_commit (git's vc..HEAD set over all parents); a vc that is not an ancestor of HEAD stays unverified with the existing reason texts; the same-commit exemption stays. Call budget per bundle, in every path including error paths: at most one git log plus at most one merge-base call per distinct verified_commit; per-sha ancestry calls plus an extra octopus call breaks it. One shape that fits: build a common base B of the distinct vcs with n-1 pairwise git merge-base calls (stderr names a bad sha), run one git log with hash and parents plus --name-only over HEAD --not B^@ (no --first-parent, no -m), and derive both ancestry (vc is in the logged set) and each concept's window (logged set minus the vc's ancestors walked through the logged parents) from that one graph. Expose one pub(crate) function in freshness.rs that says whether an anchor covers a repo path (a directory anchor covers every file under it, the current anchor_touched rule) so the cap door in kfm-3 reuses it. Tests red-first in knowledge/tests.rs: a fixture with a --no-ff merge where the vc sits on the merged branch and a second distinct vc exists, and changes that are ancestors of the vc do not make it suspect; an anchor change on the side branch after the vc, merged, makes it suspect; a test that counts git calls through an injectable runner for 1, 2 and 3 distinct vcs, one of them an unknown sha.
